To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the supply function of minority carriers from inversion layers can be expressed as a function of the surface potential, the surface carrier density, the surface Fermi level, the semiconductor band gap and the semiconductor intrinsic carrier density.
we have derived an analytical expression for the supply function of minority carriers for tunnelling into an insulator, valid in the whole range of inversion layer carrier concentrations.

the supply function for tunneled minority carriers from an inversion layer, based on the Boltzman transport equation, reduces to two terms that are in agreement with the quasi-equilibrium case for high inversion densities and with the extreme non-equilibrium case for low inversion densities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the theory of tunnelling from semiconductor surfaces.
a new approach to the modelling of tunnelling from inverted surfaces of semiconductors, based on the Boltzman transport equation.

the development of a general formulation of supply functions for tunnelling, and the application of the obtained results to the study of the electrical characteristics of metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the supply function is a function of the Fermi energy and of the quasi-Fermi level in the semiconductor and that it is independent of the quasi-Ferrmi level in the metal.

, for the particular case of the supply function of minority carriers from inverted surfaces, the Boltzmann approach is the only one able to describe the full range of possible situations, from the extreme non-equilibrium to the quasi-equilibrium limit.
the supply function is the most important quantity in the theory of hot carrier transport, and the one that has been least studied and understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new model of the supply function for minority carrier tunnelling from an inversion layer.

we have derived an analytical expression for the supply function for tunneled carriers from an inversion layer, which can be used for the analysis of any kind of semiconductor device, where the tunnelling of carriers from an inverted surface is relevant.
we have proposed a general expression for the supply function, which is valid for all cases, and is consistent with the existing expressions for the extreme cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supply function is not necessarily given by a Fermi-Dirac distribution.
the supply function is a function of the applied gate bias, which is not the case for the commonly used expression.
the supply function is a generalization of the Fermi-Dirac distribution, and can be used for any kind of tunnelling from a surface, provided that the Boltzmann equation holds.
